mes: We enter the old observatory.
Dust hangs in the moonlight.
I inspect the brass door.
A hidden lock clicks beneath your fingers.
I listen at the door before opening it.
Beyond it, a pendulum ticks with no visible clock.
I mark the route on my map and search the desk.
Under a stack of star charts you find a copper key stamped with a raven.
I pocket the key and inspect the rotating ceiling.
The constellations drift until one points toward the eastern stair.
I ask the caretaker's portrait what happened here.
The painted caretaker whispers that the observatory remembers every promise.
I promise to return the stolen lens and approach the stair.
The pendulum stops, and a cold draft rises from below.
I light a lantern and count the steps.
There are thirteen steps, then a landing with a cracked mirror.
I cover the mirror and listen for footsteps.
A distant door closes somewhere beneath the observatory.
I follow the draft toward the archives.
The archive shelves are labeled with years that have not happened yet.
I look for the raven seal among the future records.
One ledger bears the same raven seal as the key in your pocket.
I open the ledger carefully.
Its first page describes your arrival in precise detail.
I tear out the page and hide it.
The remaining pages turn blank, but the ink stains your fingertips.
I search for a way back to the central dome.
A brass compass spins, then settles toward a narrow service tunnel.
I take the service tunnel with the lantern raised.
The tunnel opens behind the clockwork orrery beneath the dome.
I fit the copper key into the orrery's raven-shaped lock.
The mechanism hums and reveals a glass lens suspended in blue light.
I retrieve the lens and prepare to keep my promise.
The portrait smiles for the first time as dawn reaches the observatory.
I carry the lens back to the caretaker's portrait.
The painted figure bows and the eastern windows unlock.
I place the lens where it belongs and watch the stars fade.
The observatory settles into silence, its clocks finally keeping ordinary time.
I leave a note promising to return at the next new moon.
A raven circles once above the dome and disappears into the morning mist.
